thread.title: ASIA MARKETS: Most Asian Markets Gain To Open November, With Only Japan Lagging

author: morningstar.com
title: ASIA MARKETS: Most Asian Markets Gain To Open November, With Only Japan Lagging
text:
By Dow Jones Newswires
Telecom stocks dive in Japan; Chinese stocks surge, led by Apple supplies
After a roller-coaster October, Asian stock markets largely started November with widespread gains with only Japan as the notable exception.
The Nikkei closed down nearly 1.1% amid caution over U.S. trade policies and the upcoming U.S. midterm elections. The telecom sector fell some 6%, by far the worst among 33 Topix sectors, after NTT DoCoMo said it would cut mobile service charges. Shares in NTT DoCoMo (9437.TO) were down 14% while fellow telecom KDDI (9433.TO) dropped 16% and SoftBank Group (9984.TO) sank 8.1%. Panasonic (6752.TO) was also sharply down.
Meanwhile, Chinese stocks surged Thursday, with Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index jumping 1.8%. Apple Inc. (AAPL) suppliers Sunny Optical (2382.HK) and AAC Tech (2018.HK) rose 7.3% and 7.8%, respectively, a day after Apple unveiled new computers and iPads. Country Garden (2007.HK) and China Overseas Land (0688.HK) rose 9.2% and 4.7%, respectively, after what UOB Kay Hian analyst Ivan Ip called an upbeat assessment on mainland China's construction recovery from Wednesday's PMI reading. Among the losers, CLP Holdings (0002.HK) was down 1.3% and Power Assets (0006.HK) slipped 1.3%.
Mainland China benchmarks continued slightly higher, as the latest Politburo meeting called for "healthy development" of the capital market. The Shanghai Composite ticked up 0.1%. The smaller-cap Shenzhen Composite was up 0.9%, following its seventh straight monthly decline. Some AI-related names popped, boosted by President Xi Jinping's pep talk, while infrastructure stocks outperformed the boarder market.
Australia's ASX 200 rose 0.2%, as BHP Billiton (BHP.AU) rose after announcing a plan to give $10.4 billion from its shale sale to investors via an equally split buyback and special dividend. Stocks in New Zealand rose as well.
Taiwan's Taiex gained 0.4% despite fears that the country's economic slowdown could be worse than it seems, after third-quarter GDP grew 2.28% year-over-year, slower than the previous quarter's 3.3% expansion. Benchmark indexes in South Korea , Singapore and Malaysia all posted solid gains.
